summary: Retrieval eval harness: a handful of canonical comparative-religion queries (the One, non-dual awareness, divine names) with expected top-K cross-tradition coverage, so 'did the scoring change help?' is answerable

analysis.author: Backend Engineer
analysis.content: Building the harness FIRST as a pre-redesign baseline, ahead of fbf4652f (relaxing the depends_on I originally wired) — you want the baseline captured before scoring changes so the before/after is real. Seeded from a live local run against the real corpus (2852 chunks, 11k EXPRESSES edges). Key metrics the harness tracks: top-K distinct-tradition coverage and graph-vs-vector source mix in top-K (the redesign's success signal — under current Bug-2 scoring, graph-only candidates get flat 0.5 distance and rarely survive). Local baseline that motivated this: graph leg fires 10/12 canonical queries with ~12.5 graph-only candidates each, but the 0.5 similarity floor is a no-op on this thematically-tight corpus (max chunk-to-chunk distance 0.56), so the floor was dropped from scope.

resolution.note: Eval harness at scripts/eval-retrieval.ts runs canonical queries through retrieve() and reports top-K distinct-tradition coverage, graph/vector source mix, and per-leg diagnostics. Baseline captured (current scoring): avg 3.58 traditions/top-K, 7/12 below the 3-tradition target, graph-sourced=80% of slots, graph fired 10/12, 2/12 zero-concept. Re-run after fbf4652f to diff. Surfaced that Bug1xBug2 makes graph DOMINATE (not suppressed) — see parent 69022947 note.
